review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines row and matrix update programs (updateRow, updateMatrix), augment and advance, together with their machine realizers and polynomial-time proofs. It also proves the code-correspondence lemmas against the repo's own Edmonds–Karp development. I checked where FlowMatrix, matrixIndices and UpdateData are defined. FlowMatrix is a List (List Signed) abbreviation, matrixIndices is List.range C.length, and UpdateData is a tuple abbreviation. These are encodings for the repo's realizer/machine framework, not competing versions of a Mathlib concept. The framework is custom (Realizer, PolynomialTime), and I found no Mathlib counterpart for it. The List.range/map definitions are thin named wrappers over core list operations, and the rubric says such wrappers are not defects. I found no avoidable duplicate of an existing Mathlib, core or Batteries concept. I did not search Mathlib exhaustively for a computability-model analogue, so there is some residual uncertainty.
